subject.title: feat(cron): configurable minimum interval guardrail for recurring jobs

question: Should OpenClaw core accept `cron.minInterval` as the operator-facing cadence guardrail, with unset/0 preserving shipped behavior and configured values rejecting or pacing fast recurring jobs?
rationale: This adds a new core config surface and deliberate fail-closed behavior for configured recurring schedules, which is a product and compatibility choice even though the implementation is opt-in.

options.title: Accept Default-Off Guardrail After Fixes
options.body: Keep this core config surface, require the generated docs-map/rebase fix and fresh exact-head proof, then merge with the documented opt-in compatibility contract.

options.title: Narrow To Advisory Behavior
options.body: Reject enforcement for now and revive a warning-only path like the closed high-frequency schedule PR if maintainers prefer no configured schedule rejection.

options.title: Defer The Config Surface
options.body: Pause this PR and keep the broader cron guardrail work under the existing umbrella issues until a fuller policy is chosen.

recommendation.title: Accept Default-Off Guardrail After Fixes
recommendation.body: Keep this core config surface, require the generated docs-map/rebase fix and fresh exact-head proof, then merge with the documented opt-in compatibility contract.
